note: Conformance vectors for the tour's two documents, GET /tour and GET
/tour/feedback. Shared, not owned: an application emits them and the harness
reads them, and neither imports the other. project-seed/tour-schema.json is
Every valid payload came out of a real emitter,
apothecary/tour.py, run on a state folder of its own: cut to the journeys and
stages a case needs, and otherwise as emitted. Each invalid case, and the
one valid case shaped as an older record, says in its why which one edit
`valid` -- an application may serve it, and a reader must read it. False
means a reader refuses it, saying why.
Adding a case is cheap, and is the right response to a document read
wrongly in the wild. Removing one needs a reason.

tries.heading: Slice, in printer_1's Machine, slices the piece and chooses its G-code
tries.words: printer_1's ring, Device › Open: its Machine a tab beside Pictures, below Selected, and ⊞ Windows › Print opens its Print from here, a tab beside it in a column already four stacks deep. It lists the pieces of the garage under makes; disc_1 chosen, its Slice slices it for printer_1, the slicer's log in the card while it runs. The G-code it kept is chosen in the card's files, saying what it was sliced from and for which printer, and the card lists what the slice used -- each value from the printer's profile, a piece declaring none -- with the slicer's estimate. Print is maximised here from its stack, so the whole card is seen.

stages.title: Numbers
stages.words: its numbers as controls in Parameters: staged, checked, then Apply in Selected

tries.heading: Part › Edit opens the part's editor at what is drawn
tries.words: The universe, /viewer/sites/apothecary, where every part is a leaf: calibration_cube's row in Site, its ring, Part › Edit, then Panels › Windows › Part view: its parameters in Parameters, under Selected. They start from what is drawn, the part's own STL as its params sidecar records it, and beside the envelope the part declares is what that STL measures. Nothing marks it: it is the saved part. The view is brought to it by hand, Shift+drag and the wheel, as the universe frames a whole shelf of parts. A slider is the next step.

tries.heading: A size dragged is checked once the slider rests
tries.words: The size slider dragged through 5 values without a pause: its line in the part's SCAD, in the editor below, rewritten as it moved, its comment kept -- the text and the controls are one draft. One check, once it rests, against the part's own model, and the envelope it would produce. Nothing is rendered yet; Apply is the next step.
tries.shown:
1 change staged, valid → 30.00 × 30.00 × 30.00 mm
size = 30;              // [10:1:50] Cube size in mm

tries.heading: Apply draws the variant, marked as not saved
tries.words: Apply: the text rendered, its size in it and nothing passed beside it, into the cache of variants, and drawn in this tab at that size, grown from where the part stood on the floor rather than centred on the envelope it had, and measured beside the envelope the part declares, Selected's Footprint following it. The editor's amber edge and its words, and an amber dot over the part in the world, say it is an applied variant and not the saved part; the status line says so too.
tries.shown:
calibration_cube regenerated: an applied variant, not saved; Part › Save keeps it in git
envelope 30.00 × 30.00 × 30.00 mm · measured 30.00 × 30.00 × 30.00 mm
